25-(Oh)D3, PGE2, and 24,25 - (Oh)2D3 mobilized Ca2 + from the endoplasmatic reticulum, 1,25(OH)2D3 from the mitochondria, while PTH mobilized Ca2 from the endoplsmatic reticulum and the extracellular space.

1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3, 25-hydroxvitamin D3 and 24,25-dihydroyvitamin D3 increase the cytosolic Ca2+ level in confluent osteoblastic cells by mobilizing Ca from different intracellular stores.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vitamin D in the modulation of the [Ca2+]I of mouse osteoblast-like cells in vitro.
the role of calcium in osteoblast cells.
the effect of vitamin D3 on the cytosolic Ca2+ concentration.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

all four vitamin D metabolites (1,25-(O H)2D3; 25-(OH)-D3, 1 alpha-hydroxy-25-(OH)-vitamin D3, and 24,25-dihydroxycho- lecalciferol) as well as PTH and PGE2 increase [Ca2+] in osteoblasts, but that each vitamin D metabolite has a different pattern of action.

the 1,25(OH)2D3-induced increase in [Ca]i is the result of Ca2+ influx through voltage-dependent Ca2+ channels and Ca2+ release from the ER, whereas PTH-induced [Ca]i increase is mainly due to Ca2+ influx.

the 25-hydroxylated vitamin D metabolites, PGE2, PTH, and the 24R-hydroxylase metabolite, 24, 25-dihydroxycholescalciferol, all mobilize Ca2+ from the ER. 1 alpha, 25-dioxygenase metabolite of vitamin D3, mobilized Ca2+, 30% from the ER and the remaining 70% from extracellular sources.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the three vitamin D metabolites and PTH induce an immediate increase in [Ca 2+]i, which is due mainly to an influx of Ca2+ from the extracellular fluid.
1,25-D3 and PTH induced an increase in [Ca]i mainly due to an influx of extracellular Ca, whereas 25-D3 and 24,25D2 increased [Ca]i by releasing Ca from the ER.

1,25 -(OH)2D and PTH increase [Ca2+] in osteoblastic cells by a dual mechanism involving release of Ca2+ from the ER and Ca2+ influx. 24, 25-(OH)(2)D3 and 25-(OH)-D3 increase [Ca2+](i) by release of Ca2+, mainly from the ER and the mitochondria.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of 1, 25-dihydroxycholeciferol (1.25 (OH) 2 D3) and parathyroid hormone on the cytosolic calcium levels of mouse osteoblast cells is mediated through calcium influx from outside the cell.

the effects of 1, 25-(OH)(2) D(3) on the cytosolic Ca(2+) concentration ([Ca(2+)](i)) of confluent mouse calvarial osteoblasts is mainly due to an increase in Ca(2+) influx from the extracellular space.
vitamin D3 metabolite-induced changes in [Ca2+](i) in confluent mouse calvarial osteoblasts are mediated by multiple mechanisms.
